Subject: PayMorrow TTFT worksheet + pilot asks (SSE vs WebSocket, chunk cadence)

Hi Elena / team,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on product intent and the critical perf goals. Per our discussion I captured the specifics below so we have a clear acceptance path for a pilot focused on live chat latency and streaming UX. Please review and flag anything missing.

Summary of ask (from your side):
- Serve interactive chat for 1k concurrent users at peak (expected initial ramp to 150 concurrent)
- Target TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 120 ms median on short prompts (<= 30 tokens) and 95th percentile <= 250 ms across US users
- Streaming response preferred (SSE) for UI progressive render; fallback to websocket if needed
- Chunk cadence goal: 100–250 ms between chunks for long responses to keep perceived latency low
- Max end-to-end tail latency for final response <= 700 ms for typical 200-token outputs

Initial Redwood proposal (what we can commit for pilot):
- Pilot environment: single-region (us-west) dedicated pool, reserved 4xA100-equivalent GPUs for 2-week run
- Default model variant: open checkpoint with q4 quantization we validated for interactive workloads
- Network SLO: example TTFT median <= 120 ms, 95p <= 280 ms (we'll iterate tuning); concurrency policy with token-aware batching to preserve TTFT
- Streaming: SSE by default; we'll surface a WebSocket option if your client prefers binary framing or bi-directional control

Operational asks from PayMorrow (items to unblock pilot):
1) A sample traffic capture (anonymized) or representative prompt set for 2000 sessions
2) A short list of client platform constraints (browser versions, mobile vs desktop split)
3) Preferred telemetry access: HubSpot org id + a read-only log/S3 for pilot traces

Attachments: pilot_scope_runbook.md (scope + success criteria), paymorrow_perf_targets.xlsx (your targets), chunking_probe_results.csv (our pre-probe results)

Next steps / owners:
- Elena: confirm the sample prompt set and procurement contact for the NDA (by 2026-09-03)
- Procurement: share PO template and any legal redlines we should expect (by 2026-09-07)
- Karhtik (cc): will schedule a 30-min tech sync to agree on telemetry and toggles (I'll let him propose times)
- I'll draft a brief pilot runbook and share for sign-off by EOD Monday (9/1).

Thanks — excited to get this moving.

Best,

Thanks both — quick technical follow-up from the infra side. I captured configuration suggestions and a few clarifying questions so the pilot will exercise the correct failure modes.

Quick config suggestions (pilot-only):
- Concurrency shaping: start with per-GPU concurrency target at 40 requests/sec (short prompts) and increase by 20% per day during a 5-day ramp; this keeps queueing minimal for TTFT.
- Request routing: pin interactive sessions to a low-latency pool; use token-aware batching with a 10 ms batching window for best median TTFT.
- Streaming path: SSE default with chunk sizes of ~64–128 bytes (encoding dependent) and target inter-chunk cadence of 120–200 ms. For clients that prefer websocket, we can enable it but note it adds ~10–30 ms on avg for handshake under some browsers.
- Cache priming: if you have predictable prompts, enable prefix caching for hot sessions to drop TTFT by ~25% on median.

Questions we need from PayMorrow to size success criteria precisely:
1) Do you have a sample 95p target for final response latency (not just TTFT)? You mentioned 700 ms as a desirable cap — please confirm target and acceptable exceptions.
2) Can we access a synthetic client (headless browser) for the pilot so we can measure first-byte render with the same instrument? If not, we will provide an SDK snippet you can embed.
3) Are there any long-polling or reverse-proxy layers in front of the client that might buffer streaming chunks (we need to know to avoid mis-attributing chunk cadence issues)?

Operational notes: we'll collect per-request traces (TTFT, total tokens, batching delay, GPU queue time) and publish a nightly report to the shared drive. We can also push Grafana dashboards if you want live metrics.

Proposed tech sync: Wed 2026-09-02 10:00 AM PT — I can send an invite.
